[PATH:empirical] Quasi-experimental studies using variation in H-1B visa lotteries or regional visa caps to estimate short-run effects on low-skill native employment in high-dynamism, low-mobility urban areas. — Provides causal identification of high-skill immigration effects on low-skill labor market outcomes, directly testing the hypothesis in the specified context.

[PATH:theoretical] Search and matching labor market models with heterogeneous firms and workers, calibrated to urban developed economies with low geographic mobility and high firm dynamism. — Allows simulation of short-term equilibrium adjustments in employment and wages, isolating mechanisms (e.g., complementarity vs. displacement) under the specified conditions.

[PATH:literature] Meta-analysis of recent empirical literature on immigration impacts on native low-skill employment, focusing on studies that report heterogeneous effects by regional firm dynamism and labor mobility. — Synthesizes existing evidence to assess whether the hypothesized negative effect is consistently found or refuted in relevant contexts, and identifies gaps in the literature.
